data.title: HEADWATER EXPLORATION INC. AND TRIBUTARY EXPLORATION INC. ANNOUNCE COMPLETION OF PREVIOUSLY ANNOUNCED PLAN OF ARRANGEMENT WITH TAMARACK VALLEY ENERGY LTD.
data.description:
CALGARY, AB, Nov. 19, 2026 /CNW/ -- Headwater Exploration Inc. ("Headwater") () and Tributary Exploration Inc. ("Tributary") are pleased to announce the successful completion of the previously announced plan of arrangement with Tamarack Valley Energy Ltd. ("Tamarack"), pursuant to which, among other things, Tamarack acquired all of the issued and outstanding common shares of Headwater in an all-stock transaction (the "Arrangement") creating a premier North American oil company with top-tier profitability and the unmatched position as the only publicly-traded Clearwater focused producer.

As part of the Arrangement, certain assets, including Headwater's Mannville-stack exploratory mineral rights in Alberta, prospective thermal heavy oil opportunities at Handel, Saskatchewan and the legacy McCully natural gas assets in New Brunswick, collectively valued at approximately $100.7 million, were transferred from Headwater and Tamarack to Tributary.

Pursuant to the Arrangement, former Headwater shareholders and Tamarack shareholders became shareholders of Tributary. In addition, former Headwater shareholders received Tributary share purchase warrants (an "Arrangement Warrants") with each Arrangement Warrant entitling the holder thereof to acquire one Tributary common share at an exercise price of $2.10 per Tributary common share for a period of 60 days following closing of the Arrangement. The exercise price of the Arrangement Warrants reflects the five-to-one consolidation of Tributary shares that was completed as part of the Arrangement.

Tributary is also completing a non-brokered private placement financing (the "Tributary Private Placement") of approximately 14.3 million units (each unit consisting of one Tributary common share and one Tributary share purchase warrant) at a price of $2.10 per unit, for aggregate gross proceeds of up to $30 million. Directors, officers, employees and consultants of Tributary and certain other investors have subscribed for units under the Tributary Private Placement, which is expected to be completed in two tranches. The first tranche of the Tributary Private Placement closed immediately following the closing of the Arrangement with the second and final tranche expected to close on or around November 30, 2026.

Tributary will be managed by the former management team of Headwater and the Tributary Board of Directors will consist of former members of the Board of Directors of Headwater.

In connection with closing of the Arrangement, Tributary has entered into a credit agreement with the National Bank of Canada and BMO Capital Markets for credit facilities with an aggregate limit of $35 million.

The Toronto Stock Exchange (the "TSX") has conditionally approved the listing of the Tributary common shares under the symbol "TBX" and the Arrangement Warrants under the symbol "TBX.WT". Listing remains subject to Tributary fulfilling all of the requirements of the TSX, and trading is expected to commence on or about November 23, 2026. It is anticipated that the Headwater common shares will be delisted from trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange concurrently with the listing of the Tributary common shares.

data.title: UK launches latest renewables auction in drive to decarbonise
data.description:
The British government on Thursday announced its latest auction for renewable power, seeking bids from clean energy project developers as part of its drive to decarbonise the electricity sector by 2030 and help lower consumer bills.

  • The government has said clean homegrown power will lower bills in the long term

  • Britain's quarterly domestic energy price cap is expected to rise by about 26% in January, analysts at Cornwall Insight said on Wednesday, as the US-Israeli war on Iran keeps wholesale energy prices elevated

  • Seeking to procure new wind and solar developments, Britain holds regular auctions to set the budget of projects

  • The government said it would set a final budget once all bids have been submitted, a change from when they used to set a budget beforehand

  • Over the last two years, auctions have secured enough clean electricity to power more than 20 million homes, the government said

  • Earlier in November RWE and US private equity firm KKR agreed to invest around £12 billion in offshore wind projects in Britain

data.title: China Medical System's Innovative Oral Drug for Vitiligo, Povorcitinib Enrolls First Patient in China Phase III Clinical Trial
data.description:
SHENZHEN, Nov 19, 2026 - (ACN Newswire) - China Medical System Holdings Limited ('CMS' or the 'Group', 867.HK/8A8.SG) is pleased to announce that its subsidiary, Dermavon Holdings Limited ('Dermavon', an innovative pharmaceutical company specialized in skin health which is applying for a separate listing on the Main Board of The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong Limited), has enrolled the first patient in the China Phase III clinical trial of its innovative oral JAK1 inhibitor Povorcitinib Phosphate Tablets ('povorcitinib' or the 'Product') for the treatment of vitiligo on 19 November 2026.

The trial is a multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III clinical study evaluating the efficacy and safety of povorcitinib in Chinese adult patients with non-segmental vitiligo. Led by Professor Li Chunying of the First Affiliated Hospital of Air Force Medical University, the study is planned to be conducted at approximately 44 clinical research centers across China and is expected to enroll approximately 174 patients with non-segmental vitiligo.

The Product has previously completed a series of clinical trials related to pharmacokinetics and bioequivalence in healthy participants in China, and has been included in the list of Breakthrough Therapeutic Drugs by the Center for Drug Evaluation of the National Medical Products Administration of the People's Republic of China ('NMPA'). This certification has the potential to accelerate its development and review process. The enrollment of the first patient in this China Phase III clinical trial marks a pivotal stage in the Product's clinical development in China and lays a foundation for further evaluating its efficacy and safety in Chinese patients with vitiligo.

Addressing Unmet Clinical Needs in Vitiligo with Novel and Differentiated Treatment Options

Vitiligo is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by depigmentation of the skin. It is estimated that there are approximately 10.3 million vitiligo patients in China and non-segmental vitiligo patients account for approximately 8.2 million[1]. Currently, treatment options are limited for vitiligo patients who require systemic therapy, and their clinical treatment needs remain inadequately met.

Overactivity of certain proinflammatory cytokines that signal through the JAK-STAT pathway, is believed to drive inflammation and contribute to the pathogenesis and progression of vitiligo. Incyte has announced that Phase III clinical studies outside China of the oral JAK1 inhibitor Povorcitinib Phosphate Tablets in adults with non-segmental vitiligo have met the primary endpoints[2]. If approved in China, the Product has the potential to provide a new oral treatment option for patients with non-segmental vitiligo and, together with Dermavon's commercialized innovative drug Lumirix' (ruxolitinib phosphate cream), provide vitiligo patients with comprehensive and diversified treatment options, from precise topical intervention to systemic treatment.

Focusing on major skin diseases such as vitiligo, atopic dermatitis and psoriasis, Dermavon has developed an innovative product portfolio covering different disease stages and clinical needs. The enrollment of the first patient in the Phase III clinical trial of povorcitinib in China represents another important milestone in Dermavon's advancement of local clinical development for global innovative drugs. Going forward, Dermavon will continue to leverage its strong global R&D partnerships and clinical development capabilities in China to accelerate the translation of innovation into clinical application and bring more professional and differentiated treatment options to patients with skin diseases in China.

More Information About Povorcitinib Phosphate Tablets

Povorcitinib is a selective oral small-molecule JAK1 inhibitor, with compound and use patents in certain countries/regions in the Territory. In addition to vitiligo, the Product has also demonstrated development potential in other indications. Incyte is conducting Phase III clinical trials of povorcitinib for the treatment of prurigo nodularis (PN) in several countries outside China, and has obtained European Commission approval for hidradenitis suppurativa (HS). Dermavon may also consider initiating clinical development of the Product in China for the treatment of additional skin-related diseases.

A subsidiary of Dermavon entered into a Collaboration and License Agreement (the 'License Agreement') for povorcitinib on 31 March 2024 with Incyte, obtaining an exclusive license to research, develop, register and commercialize the Product in Mainland China, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Macao Special Administrative Region, Taiwan Region and eleven Southeast Asian countries (the 'Territory') and a non-exclusive license to manufacture the Product in the Territory. The subsidiary of Dermavon has sublicensed the relevant rights of povorcitinib in the Territory other than Mainland China to China Medical System Holdings Limited (excluding Dermavon and its subsidiaries).

About CMS

CMS is an innovative pharmaceutical company focused on the identification, building, and full lifecycle management of differentiated specialty pharmaceuticals. With a dual-engine approach of in-house R&D and collaborative R&D, and leveraging its core capability to build markets and brands from the ground up, the Group enables each medicine to fully realize both its clinical value and commercial value.

CMS has established an end-to-end capability loop across the full product lifecycle-precisely identifying quality innovation targets, matching them with optimal development pathways, and efficiently advancing clinical development and registration; developing medical strategies aligned with clinical needs, and driving scaled clinical adoption through a professional academic promotion system and network.

CMS focuses on advantaged specialties including cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic, central nervous system, gastroenterology, ophthalmology, and skin health. Through professional academic promotion and academic resources across multiple disease areas, CMS has built sustainable scale advantages in specialties, with its skin health business becoming a leading player in its segment. Meanwhile, CMS continues to strengthen its international replication capabilities, validating the transferability of its business model in emerging markets such as Southeast Asia and the Middle East, and injecting long-term momentum for the Group's high-quality, sustainable development.

data.title: Canada Producer Prices Rise Again in October, Buoyed by Energy Products
data.description:
By Robb M. Stewart

OTTAWA--Canadian manufactured goods prices continued to climb last month as the Iran war again drove up energy and petroleum products.

Statistics Canada's industrial product price index increased 0.3% in October from the month before, a softer advance than the upwardly revised 1.5% rise that in September. Compared with a year earlier, prices were 12.6% higher, a 25th consecutive annual increase.

Still, prices for raw materials bought by manufacturers operating in the country fell 1% in the latest month, though were up 23.5% compared with last year.

The steady rise in producer prices adds to signs of cost pressures since the start of the Iran conflict, which has elevated prices for crude oil and other commodities and added to economic uncertainty.

Prices for energy and petroleum products in Canada increased 1.2% in October after an 8.6% gain in September. Excluding energy, industrial product prices edged up 0.1% during October and were 6.7% above the same month last year, the national data agency said.

A rise in diesel fuel prices drove the increase, followed by light fuel oils, while finished motor gasoline prices declined 1.2% and helped moderate the advance in energy. Compared with a year prior, diesel fuel increased 93.3%, gasoline was up 50.2%, and light fuel oils climbed 100.3%.

Prices also rose month-on-month for chemicals and chemical products, and for fabricated metal products and construction materials, Statistics Canada said. There was a drop in prices for primary non-ferrous and primary ferrous metals.

The industrial product price index measures the prices that manufacturers in Canada receive once their goods leave the plant. It doesn't reflect the final prices consumers pay for goods on store shelves.

Consumer price inflation has been at or above the upper end of the Bank of Canada's 1%-to-3% control range for the last four months, holding at 3.1% in October. The central bank has increasingly focused on the rise in the outlook for inflation, and has forecast that annual inflation will accelerate to 3.5% by the end of the year and remain above 3% through much of 2028 before gradually cooling.

Worries that elevated energy prices will spread through the economy more broadly prompted the bank to lifts its policy interest rate in late October. Deputy Gov. Toni Gravelle in a speech this week said the longer oil prices remain high the less likely it is companies won't pass that along, and already there have been signs of that spillover.

The consumer-price index and industrial product data are the last inflation gauges the Bank of Canada's governing council will see before its next policy meeting on Dec. 9.

Prices for raw materials in Canada, which track costs paid by manufacturers, were driven down in October by metal ores, concentrates and scrap. This offset a rise in crude energy products costs. excluding crude energy products, raw materials costs fell by 3.3% between September and October.

The fall in ores, concentrates and scrap was led by lower prices for gold, silver and platinum group metals. Silver ores, concentrates and mill bullion fell 9.8%, while gold ores, concentrates and mill bullion decreased 3.8%, the data agency said.

data.title: Arkansas Launches Statewide Digital Services App, Bringing More than 50 Government Services to Residents with Tyler Technologies
data.description:
Tyler Technologies, Inc. () today announced the successful launch of MyArkansas, a new mobile application from the Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration (DFA) that gives residents convenient access to more than 50 state services in one location.

MyArkansas is the first statewide government mobile app in Arkansas, serving more than 3 million residents. Available through the Apple App Store and Google Play, MyArkansas enables residents to access services using their Login.gov accounts. Residents can use the app to book lodging at Arkansas State Parks, purchase hunting and fishing licenses, renew vehicle registrations, check office wait times, request vital records, and apply for an Education Freedom Account. The app also provides updates and notifications related to emergency preparedness, license renewals, tax deadlines, and benefits eligibility.

Arkansas selected Tyler through a competitive RFP process, citing the company’s technical capabilities, proven experience delivering resident engagement solutions in other states, and its longstanding partnership with Arkansas DFA. The partnership spans three decades, with Tyler supporting the state’s efforts to modernize technology and improve service delivery.

“Tyler helps state and local governments like the Arkansas DFA provide more connected digital experiences, making it easier for residents to find information, complete transactions, and engage with government on their terms,” said Liz Thomas, president of Tyler’s State & Federal Group. “We look forward to continuing our work with the state as it builds on this foundation to expand digital access to services across Arkansas.”

About Tyler Technologies, Inc.

Tyler Technologies () is a leading provider of technology solutions purpose-built exclusively for the public sector. Tyler’s end-to-end solutions empower local, state, and federal government entities to operate efficiently and transparently with residents and each other. By connecting data and processes across disparate systems, Tyler’s solutions strengthen the core operations of government and help agencies turn insight into action for their communities. With more than 50,000 installations across 16,000 client locations, Tyler serves clients in all 50 states, Canada, the Caribbean, Australia, and other international locations. Tyler has been recognized numerous times for growth and innovation, including on Government Technology’s GovTech 100 list. More information about Tyler Technologies, an S&P 500 company headquartered in Plano, Texas, can be found at tylertech.com.

data.title: Wheat up 5-9 cents, corn up 1-2 cents, soybeans up 2-6 cents
data.description:
The following are expectations for the resumption of grain and soy complex trading at the Chicago Board of Trade at 8:30 a.m. CDT (1330 GMT) on Thursday.

WHEAT - Up 5 to 9 cents per bushel

  • Chicago wheat futures recovered from four-month lows, as an easing in the US dollar index and a steadying in crude oil prices helped stem broad-based commodity selling.

  • An apparent absence of diplomatic progress towards de-escalation in Russia's war in Ukraine, after three-way talks between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China, also underpinned grain markets, traders said.

  • Russian President Vladimir Putin ruled out negotiations for a Black Sea ceasefire after Ukraine destroyed part of a bridge linking Russia to Crimea, dampening hopes of progress towards de-escalation in the conflict.

  • The US Department of Agriculture reported net export sales of US wheat in the week ended November 12 at 344,800 metric tons in the current marketing year, within a range of trade expectations for 200,000 to 400,000 tons.

  • A group of South Korean flour mills has issued an international tender to purchase around 100,000 metric tons of milling wheat to be sourced from the United States only, European traders said on Thursday.

  • CBOT December soft red winter wheat was last 8-1/4 cents higher at $5.78-1/4 per bushel; KC December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) was last 14-3/4 cents higher at $6.24 per bushel and Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) was last up 11 cents at $6.40-1/4 per bushel.

CORN - Up 1 to 2 cents per bushel

  • CBOT corn futures also firmed, following wheat higher.

  • A weaker US dollar is bullish for Chicago grain futures, as it can make agricultural goods less expensive for importers to purchase. (FRX/)

  • The US Department of Agriculture reported net export sales of US corn in the week ended November 12 at 1,588,100 metric tons for the current marketing year, within a range of trade expectations for 1.2 million to 2 million tons.

  • US weekly ethanol stocks increased, while output ticked lower, the Energy Information Administration said on Wednesday.

  • The International Grains Council has lowered its forecast for 2026/27 global corn production by 6 million metric tons to 1.301 billion tons, it said on Thursday.

  • December corn was last 1 cent higher at $4.36-1/2 per bushel.

SOYBEANS - Up 2 to 6 cents per bushel

  • CBOT soybeans turned higher, breaking a three-day slide in prices, on technical buying and a steadying in the crude oil markets.

  • The oilseed, processed for biodiesel fuel, has been pressured by a drop in oil prices this week, before crude firmed on Thursday.

  • Exporters sold 200,844 metric tons of US soybeans to Mexico for delivery in the 2026/27 marketing year, the US Department of Agriculture said in its daily reporting system.

  • Separately, USDA reported net export sales of US soybeans in the week ended November 12 at 1,501,000 metric tons for the current marketing year, within a range of trade expectations for 1 million to 2 million tons.

  • But favorable weather in Brazil has maintained supply pressure on the soybean market after what is estimated to be a record US harvest.

  • CBOT January soybeans were 6 cents higher at $12.22-3/4 per bushel.

data.title: Amundi CIO says not bearish on France bonds, AI at the start of repricing
data.description:
Key points:
  • Amundi's Mortier says neutral on French, Japan bonds
  • Mortier says favours bonds from Australia, Norway, Switzerland
  • Core AI sector is at start of a repricing, says Mortier

By Sophie Kiderlin and Javi West Larrañaga

Amundi, Europe's largest asset manager, is not bearish on French government bonds and believes the bar for European Central Bank intervention to calm bond market turbulence is high, Group Chief Investment Officer Vincent Mortier said on Thursday.

French bond yields have risen sharply this year on concerns over the country's ability to pass a budget and rein in its high deficit, while recent protests and an upcoming election have added to investor unease.

"We are neutral on French debt," Mortier said on a 2027 outlook call. "So, we are not bearish, we are not, we are just neutral."

The premium investors demand to hold French 10-year bonds over safe-haven German debt is around 150 basis points, up from around 85 bps at the start of September and 70 bps at the end of 2025 (DE10FR10=RR).

"If the spread widens to 200 bps, we would probably buy," Mortier said, adding the ECB would only step in if the gap was "much higher" than current levels.

"It's very clear that 150 or 200 bps is not at all distressed and is not an issue."

The ​ECB's Transmission Protection Instrument allows it to buy bonds from any member state facing an "unwarranted, disorderly" tightening in financing conditions, but policymakers have indicated France should tackle its debt problems through fiscal consolidation rather than rely on central bank support.

SOME BONDS ATTRACTIVE

Mortier said Amundi, which manages nearly €2.6 trillion ($2.9 trillion) in assets, favoured the bonds of countries with relatively low debt-to-GDP ratios, such as Norway, Australia and Switzerland, and preferred short-dated debt.

He also said he was neutral on Japanese government bonds (JGBs).

"Maybe we will be long soon, because at such a level, we believe that there will be some renewed interest from local investors to buy JGBs as an alternative," he said.

On European equities, Mortier said Amundi was less bullish for 2027 than it had been this year, warning that positive earnings momentum was likely to fade.

"There are lots of parameters to contemplate because energy prices are very volatile, euro/dollar is very unstable, European growth is uneven," Mortier said.

Robust earnings and a fall in oil prices helped push Europe's STOXX 600 index to record highs last week.

Among emerging markets, India stood out, Mortier said.

An AI-driven rally in emerging markets has drawn foreign capital away from India in recent years.

"There was this narrative in the marketplace, and lots of foreigners were selling Indian equities, that India is an AI loser," said Mortier. "It's totally stupid, because India, through adoption of AI, can become an AI winner."

More broadly, he said investors had been "obsessed" with core AI companies but that focus would shift in 2027. Amundi instead favours sectors using AI to drive productivity and transformation, including pharmaceuticals, biotech and some industrial companies.

Addressing recent volatility in tech and AI stocks, Mortier said the core AI sector was at the start of a repricing, but that this was "standard" after exceptional momentum.

data.title: Wingspire Equipment Finance Commits $30 Million to Support New Contract Wins
data.description:
Wingspire Equipment Finance announced a $30 million equipment financing commitment for a sponsor-backed industrial services company.

Structured as an equipment line, the financing supports the acquisition of material handling and transport equipment, dump trucks, and related assets. The capital commitment gives management certainty of funding when bidding on new customer contracts.

Wingspire Equipment Finance also provided progress funding to support equipment procurement as the company prepared to fulfill its customer obligations. By financing 100% of the capital equipment needs associated with new customers, the facility helps the portfolio company preserve liquidity and enhances the sponsor’s return on equity.

The transaction required a financing approach that addressed the complexity of the sponsor-backed company’s original carve-out acquisition. Wingspire Equipment Finance worked with the company to establish an equipment financing solution aligned with its operating requirements and growth opportunities.

“For our client, winning new business requires confidence that equipment capital will be available to take on new contracts,” said Michael Grande, Managing Director of Wingspire Equipment Finance. “We structured a committed line with progress funding to help them secure the necessary assets and fulfill their customer commitments.”

The recent transaction demonstrates Wingspire Equipment Finance’s ability to structure an equipment financing solution around complex ownership transitions and the capital requirements of sponsor-backed industrial services businesses.

About Wingspire Equipment Finance:

Wingspire Equipment Finance is a leading provider of large transaction equipment financing solutions, empowering middle-market and private equity-backed companies with flexible and innovative capital structures. With a focus on client success and industry expertise, Wingspire Equipment Finance provides strategic capital solutions that promote long-term success for its clients. Wingspire Equipment Finance is the equipment financing arm of Wingspire Capital, a portfolio company of Blue Owl Capital Corporation (). OBDC is externally managed by Blue Owl Credit Advisors LLC, an indirect affiliate of Blue Owl Capital, Inc. (). Blue Owl Capital, Inc. is a global alternative asset manager with $330 billion of assets under management as of September 30, 2026.

Loans made or arranged pursuant to a California Financing Law license.
